newsitem.title: UK: HSBC treasurer says its bonus system not excessive.
newsitem.headline: HSBC treasurer says its bonus system not excessive.

text.p: HSBC Holdings Plc, which announced pre-tax profits of 4.52 billion pounds in 1996, said on Monday its bonus system was not excessive nor badly structured.

"As far as we are concerned, we don't believe we have a badly structured bonus approach. We avoid mechanistic formulae and bring a lot of management judgement to bear on what our appropriate bonus is in relation to performance and risk," Stephen Green, general manager group treasury told Reuters in an interview.
Green's comment were in response to questions regarding Bank of England warnings on Monday that badly structured bonuses may be encouraging traders to take more risks than their employers want.

"There is an independent process of approval of bonuses by the Remuneration Committee of the Board and we do not believe our bonuses are excessive, far from it, in relation to market trends," Green added.
"I believe strongly in the advantages of heavy dose of management judgement in determining appropriate levels of bonuses," he said.
In its latest Financial Stability Review, the Bank of England said firms must take care not to encourage bad behaviour.

"If large bonuses are paid to employees who make money but are perceived to have a cavalier attitude to compliance, it is likely to encourage similar behaviour in others," the bank said in its review.
If this were to happen, the Bank of England said an unnecessary strain would be put on a firm's other management and control systems.
On Friday the investment banking arm of one of Britain's largest banks, National Westminster Bank, reported a 50 million pound ($81 million) hole in its options trading book.

NatWest Markets is to face close scrutiny by the Securities and Futures Authority, which licenses options traders, and the Bank of England, which regulates banks generally, to establish what went wrong.
HSBC's Green said banking controls are key.

"No one can afford to be complacent. We spend a lot of effort making sure we have independent controls with independent price validation what if scenarios being calculated regularly and we regard that as very important part of our process," he added.
